provider.readme:
# Azure OpenAI
Unlike every other CBE provider, Azure OpenAI is **API-only** — there is no equivalent of `chatgpt.com` for it. Azure exposes OpenAI's models (GPT-4o, GPT-4.1, o3, etc.) as REST endpoints under your own resource deployment inside Azure. The bridge model doesn't apply; CBE talks directly to the Azure REST API with your endpoint + API key.
**First-time setup:**
1. Sign in to the [Azure Portal](https://portal.azure.com). 2. Create an "Azure OpenAI" resource in any supported region (East US, West Europe, etc. — availability varies). 3. Open the resource → "Model deployments" → deploy one or more models (e.g. `gpt-4o`, `gpt-4o-mini`, `o3-mini`). 4. Copy the resource endpoint (e.g. `https://your-name.openai.azure.com`) and one of the keys from "Keys and Endpoint". 5. Paste both into CBE Settings → Providers → Azure OpenAI.
**Models typically exposed** (whatever you've deployed in your resource):
- gpt-4o / gpt-4o-mini - gpt-4.1 / gpt-4.1-mini - o3 / o3-mini (reasoning) - text-embedding-3-large
**Billing:** pay-per-token through your Azure subscription, with enterprise SLA, regional pinning, and private-network deployment options that the consumer ChatGPT product does not offer. Cataloged here for parity even though the underlying transport is REST, not browser bridge.
